seo_description: Solo audio designer on a 4-player racing game. Procedural MetaSounds, 4-player mix management, and full audio pipeline in 12 weeks.
hero.title: Not Today, Darling!
hero.subtitle: 4-Player Chaos, One Audio Designer
hero.hook: Side-scrolling racer where grannies race, smash, and scream. I made every sound.
overview.title: Project Overview
overview.role_desc: Solo Audio Designer. Recording, sound design, music selection, and implementation. 2 programmers, 3 artists, 12 weeks.
overview.tech_desc: MetaSounds for all SFX. Engine pitch, surface changes, and collisions are all driven by real-time gameplay data. No pre-baked loops.
overview.scope_desc: Only audio person on the team. We recorded our own character voices. Built the procedural engine audio system from scratch.
overview.result_desc: Released on itch.io in May 2025. We shipped it.
systems.title: Audio Systems
systems.metasounds.title: MetaSounds Engine
systems.metasounds.desc: No looped MP3s. A MetaSounds graph where go-kart pitch and rattle shift with speed in real-time. You hear the difference when you drive from carpet onto tiles — the sound reacts instantly.
systems.architecture.title: Audio Architecture
systems.architecture.desc: With 12 weeks to ship, you need to know where your audio logic lives. One centralized manager for UI, one system for engines. Debugging took minutes, not hours.
systems.surface.title: Surface Transitions
systems.surface.desc: Abruptly switching from carpet to tiles sounded fake and glitchy. A fast crossfade between surfaces — the old sound fades out, the new one fades in. Milliseconds, but it makes driving sound professional.
mix.title: 4-Player Chaos Control
mix.desc: With 4 players crashing and screaming, important sounds got buried. I set priorities: picking up an item ducks collisions for a split second. The Wall of Death boxing bell and the 3-2-1 countdown cut through everything. Information always wins over noise.
challenges.title: Challenges & Solutions
challenges.c1_problem: With 4 players going at once, sounds stacked up and UI feedback disappeared.
challenges.c1_solution: Capped collision sounds at 4, gave each player a different EQ range, and ducked the crowd whenever UI plays.
challenges.c2_problem: Switching between asphalt, sand, and metal caused audio pops.
challenges.c2_solution: Added 150ms crossfades between surfaces. Problem gone.
challenges.c3_problem: Boost sounds were eating 160MB with 4 players active.
challenges.c3_solution: Replaced them with procedural MetaSounds patches. Went from 160MB down to under 2MB per player.
